newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-RAFTER FIGHTBACK GIVES AUSTRALIA 2-0 LEAD OVER FRANCE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-RAFTER FIGHTBACK GIVES AUSTRALIA 2-0 LEAD OVER FRANCE.

text.p: Patrick Rafter staged a stirring fightback to help Australia take a 2-0 lead over Davis Cup holders France on the first day of their world group tie on Friday.
The results left France facing the prospect of first-round defeat only nine weeks after their thrilling 3-2 victory over Sweden in the 1996 cup final.
"We've been there before and we have to dig deep again and come back," said French captain Yannick Noah, whose team recovered from 2-0 down against the Swedes to win the final.
But Australia, back in the world group after two years in regional competition, are confident of wrapping up the tie in Saturday's doubles.
Their doubles pair, Mark Woodforde and Todd Woodbridge, are the most successful twosome in action on the circuit and are the reigning Wimbledon, U.S., Australian and Olympic champions.
"Obviously it's not going to be easy because we're not playing just any doubles team," said Noah, who will pit Guy Forget and Guillaume Raoux against the Woodies.
Woodforde is also playing singles and raced past an out-of-sorts Arnaud Boetsch 6-4 6-4 6-3 on Friday in just 97 minutes.
Rafter, who came back from two sets down to beat Cedric Pioline in fierce heat in the opening rubber, was delighted with his success.
"That was probably the best and most satisfying performance I've ever had," he said.
The Australian, ranked 64th in the world to Pioline's 26, won 3-6 6-7 6-4 7-5 6-4 in four hours and 15 minutes on the White City grass court.
Rafter struggled with his serve early in the match and squandered two chances to clinch the second set, despite having led 5-1.
The third set proved decisive for the gritty Australian, whose career has suffered over the past two years through injuries and inconsistent form.
Rafter battled to save his serve in the sixth game of the third set after reaching deuce eight times and went on to break Pioline three games later.
Pioline struggled increasingly in courtside temperatures which reached 36 degrees Celsius and was unable to curb Rafter's growing enthusiasm.
"I knew he could win in five sets but that it would take a superhuman effort," Australian captain John Newcombe said.
Boetsch was unable to cope with the seamless grass-court game of an effervescent Woodforde who fully justified his selection for the singles instead of the higher-ranked Woodbridge.
"There was a tremendous amount of pressure on Arnaud after watching his team mate lose from two sets to love up and that took a bit of pressure off me," said Woodforde, 31.
